goal: Teach Year-2 physics students to turn a familiar projectile target condition into a residual f(theta)=0, interpret residual signs and a graphical zero crossing, trace scaffolded bisection and Newton updates, apply one supplied residual stopping rule, validate by substitution, and explain the physical meaning and unit of the root.

deck_context.source_summary: Week 05 uses a level-ground projectile range model to make numerical root finding physically interpretable. Students move from the target range condition to a residual, read undershoot and overshoot signs, locate a sign-changing bracket, trace bisection and Newton iterations, stop using one supplied residual tolerance, substitute the root back into the residual, and transfer the pattern to thin-lens and RC charging contexts.
deck_context.core_claim: A root is a physical input that makes a target condition true. A numerical answer is credible only when the residual is defined with units, the update is traceable, the one supplied stopping rule is satisfied, and substitution confirms the target condition.
deck_context.locked_model: Level-ground projectile range: R(theta) = (v0_mps^2/g_mps2)*sind(2*theta_deg), with v0_mps = 20 m/s, g_mps2 = 9.81 m/s^2, target_m = 35 m, theta_deg in degree, range_m in m, and residual_m = range_m - target_m.
deck_context.locked_setup: Low-angle bracket [20, 40] degree; f(20 degree) = -8.7905 m approximately; f(40 degree) = +5.1553 m approximately; Newton starting angle 25 degree; theta_scan_deg = 10:1:70; one Core stopping rule abs(residual_m) < 1e-3 m.
deck_context.locked_results: Bisection: 29.5679 degree after 13 recorded iterations with residual +4.1164e-4 m; Newton: 29.5673 degree after 4 recorded evaluations with residual -7.1308e-7 m; direct substitution at the bisection result gives range 35.0004 m and residual +4.1164e-4 m.
deck_context.bisection_trace: Iteration 1: [20,40], midpoint 30, residual +0.31194 m, keep [20,30]. Iteration 2: [20,30], midpoint 25, residual -3.7648 m, keep [25,30]. Iteration 3: [25,30], midpoint 27.5, residual -1.5993 m, keep [27.5,30]. Iteration 4: [27.5,30], midpoint 28.75, residual -0.61095 m, keep [28.75,30].
deck_context.newton_trace: Evaluation 1: theta 25 degree, residual -3.7648 m, slope 0.91488 m/degree, next angle 29.115 degree. Evaluation 2: theta 29.115 degree, residual -0.33461 m, slope 0.74939 m/degree, next angle 29.562 degree. Evaluation 3: theta 29.562 degree, residual -0.0042242 m, slope 0.73044 m/degree, next angle 29.567 degree. Evaluation 4: theta 29.567 degree, residual -7.1308e-7 m, slope 0.73019 m/degree, stop.
deck_context.transfer_contexts: Thin lens residual f(v) = 1/f - 1/u - 1/v, root v in m, residual in m^-1. RC charging residual f(t) = Vs*(1-exp(-t/(RC))) - Vthreshold, root t in s, residual in V. Do not reveal practical numerical answers on the transfer slide.
deck_context.exactness: Equations, signs, units, MATLAB variable names, MATLAB code, numerical values, trace entries, stopping rule, validation result, and transfer residual forms are strict teaching content. Do not invent, paraphrase, or change them.

core: distinguish the original physical equation from residual form f(x)=0
interpret negative, zero, and positive residuals physically
identify a zero crossing and sign-changing bracket
use one supplied residual stopping rule
validate by substituting the root into the residual
state the root's physical unit and meaning
diagnose a bad same-sign bisection bracket
working_exposure: guaranteed bracketed versus faster local method
iteration count as a limited cost measure
transfer to thin-lens and RC charging residuals

slides.title: Turn the target condition into a residual
slides.intent: Distinguish the original physical equation from the residual equation that a numerical method can drive to zero.
key_points: Original model: R(theta) = v0^2/g * sin(2 theta).
Target condition: R(theta) = 35 m.
Residual: f(theta) = R(theta) - 35 m.
A root satisfies f(theta) = 0.
slides.local_context: The residual is model range minus target range, so its unit is m. The root variable theta is an angle in degree. Make the physical model -> target -> residual zero mapping the dominant story.

slides.title: Read the residual sign as physics
slides.intent: Connect algebraic sign to undershoot, exact target, and overshoot before any iteration.
key_points: f(theta) < 0: model range is shorter than the target — undershoot.
f(theta) = 0: model range equals the target — root.
f(theta) > 0: model range is longer than the target — overshoot.
The residual is a distance mismatch in metres.
slides.local_context: Keep the sign interpretation exact. Use one horizontal physical comparison strip with three launch outcomes or target-distance states, not three unrelated decorative illustrations.

slides.title: Bisection keeps a sign change alive
slides.intent: Show the midpoint and interval-update idea in plain language before the MATLAB scaffold.
key_points: Start with endpoints whose residuals have opposite signs.
Compute the midpoint.
Evaluate the midpoint residual.
Keep the half interval whose endpoints still have opposite signs.
Repeat until the supplied residual rule is satisfied.

slides.title: Newton follows the local tangent
slides.intent: Introduce Newton as a local tangent prediction rather than a mysterious formula.
key_points: Newton uses one current angle rather than keeping an interval.
The update is new angle = current angle - residual/slope.
For degree input, the slope includes 2*pi/180.
The slope unit is metres per degree.
slides.local_context: Use a conceptual residual curve with a tangent at a current estimate, crossing the zero line at the next estimate. Preserve the exact Newton update and derivative expression from the strict asset. Do not claim Newton is always safer than bisection.
